Description: Charles II returns from exile and takes the throne.
Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor of the Romans.
The federal government rebuilds the South and passes the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments.
George I of Hanover becomes king.
Fire destroys much of the old City of London.
The Soviet Union breaks up into fifteen independent states.
The last major outbreak of bubonic plague in England kills about a fifth of London's people.
Free health care at the point of use becomes available to everyone in Britain.
King John agrees to a charter limiting royal power.
The Allies defeat Germany, Italy and Japan; the Holocaust kills six million Jews.
Fifty-one countries found the United Nations after World War II.
William Caxton sets up the first printing press in England, at Westminster.
Parliament extends the vote and redistributes seats.
Congress authorizes the forced relocation of Native American nations west of the Mississippi, leading to the Trail of Tears.
Bubonic plague kills perhaps a third or more of England's population.
The first permanent English settlement in North America is established in Virginia.
The Union Pacific and Central Pacific lines meet at Promontory Summit, Utah.
Alfred defends Wessex against the Vikings and promotes learning in English.
A Catholic conspiracy to blow up Parliament and King James is discovered.

Event: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
Description: The last Western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, is deposed.
The Allied and Central Powers fight a global war.
Napoleon Bonaparte crowns himself Emperor of the French.
Terrorist attacks on New York and Washington kill nearly 3,000 people.
Cleisthenes' reforms establish democracy in Athens.
The manufacture and sale of alcohol are banned under the 18th Amendment until its repeal.
The Ottoman Turks capture the Byzantine capital.
East Germany opens the border; Germany reunifies in 1990.
James VI of Scotland becomes James I of England, beginning the Stuart line.
Angles, Saxons and Jutes begin settling in Britain; 449 is the traditional date.
Women over 30 who meet property qualifications gain the vote.
Parliamentarians led by Oliver Cromwell defeat the Royalists.
Britain's first woman prime minister leads three Conservative governments.
Separatists from England arrive on the Mayflower and sign the Mayflower Compact.
President Lincoln declares enslaved people in the Confederate states free.
Sparta and its allies defeat Athens.
The thirteen colonies fight for and win independence from Britain.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Revolutionary Age

Description: British and Prussian forces defeat Napoleon, ending the Napoleonic Wars.
Historical Periods: Romantic Period (British); Age of the Romantic Movement

Description: The Union defeats the Confederacy, preserving the nation and ending slavery.
A religious and political war devastates central Europe.
Athens defeats a Persian invasion force.
An international exhibition at the Crystal Palace in London showcases industry.
A wave of Protestant revivals sweeps the colonies, led by preachers such as Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield.
England and France fight a long series of wars over the French throne.
Great Britain and Ireland unite as the United Kingdom.
Historical Periods: Romantic Period (British); Age of the Romantic Movement

Description: England and Scotland unite as the Kingdom of Great Britain.
The United States buys the Louisiana Territory from France, doubling the nation's size.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Federalist Age

Description: Britain and France fight for control of North America; British victory removes France from the continent.
From the Montgomery bus boycott onward, a mass movement campaigns to end segregation and secure voting rights.
The king is beheaded and England becomes a commonwealth without a monarch.
Henry VII wins the Battle of Bosworth Field and takes the throne.
British rule in India ends with partition into two independent states.
The Supreme Court rules that racial segregation in public schools is unconstitutional.
War with Mexico ends with the United States gaining California and much of the Southwest.
Uprisings spread across Europe; Marx and Engels publish The Communist Manifesto.
Lincoln is shot by John Wilkes Booth days after the Confederate surrender at Appomattox.
President Kennedy is shot in Dallas on November 22.
The first college in the English colonies is founded in Massachusetts.
The Constitutional Convention drafts a new framework of government, ratified in 1788.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Revolutionary Age

Description: The houses of Lancaster and York fight for the English crown.
The United Kingdom leaves the European Union on January 31.
European Christians capture Jerusalem.
The stock market crash of October 1929 begins the worst economic collapse in American history.
Traditional date of the first games at Olympia in Greece.
The United States defeats Spain and gains Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.
Nixon resigns the presidency over the Watergate scandal.
The Authorized Version of the Bible in English is published.
The Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic churches split.
The first women's rights convention in the United States issues the Declaration of Sentiments.
Britain declares war on Germany in September 1939; the Battle of Britain is fought in 1940.
Muhammad and his followers move from Mecca to Medina; the Islamic calendar begins.
A set of laws admits California as a free state and strengthens the Fugitive Slave Act.
The Continental Congress declares the colonies independent of Britain on July 4.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Revolutionary Age

Description: Henry VIII breaks with Rome and becomes head of the Church of England.
Traditional date of Rome's founding by Romulus.
The vote is extended to many working-class men in towns.
William of Normandy defeats Harold II at the Battle of Hastings and becomes king.
Colonists dump East India Company tea into Boston Harbor to protest the Tea Act.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Revolutionary Age

Description: Alexander of Macedon conquers an empire from Greece to India.

Event: Britain joins the European Economic Community
Description: The United Kingdom becomes a member of the EEC.
The Roman Republic gives way to the Roman Empire.
Britain declares war on Germany in August 1914.
Congress outlaws discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex or national origin.
Victoria reigns for 63 years over an expanding empire.
Accusations of witchcraft in Salem, Massachusetts, lead to the execution of twenty people.
The armies of the emperor Claudius invade, beginning nearly four centuries of Roman rule.
The French monarchy is overthrown and a republic is declared.
Johannes Gutenberg develops printing with movable metal type in Germany.
Most of Ireland becomes self-governing; Northern Ireland remains in the United Kingdom.

Event: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Description: The United States drops atomic bombs on two Japanese cities, and Japan surrenders.
The tsar is overthrown and the Bolsheviks take power.
Christopher Columbus's first voyage lands in the Caribbean.
Plague kills perhaps a third to a half of Europe's population.
England turns back the Spanish fleet sent to invade it.
Elizabeth II reigns for 70 years, the longest in British history.
Missouri enters the Union as a slave state and Maine as a free state, and slavery is barred north of 36°30′ in the Louisiana Territory.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Federalist Age

Description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first people to walk on the Moon.

Event: Darwin's On the Origin of Species
Description: Charles Darwin sets out the theory of evolution by natural selection.
Mao Zedong's Communists take power in China.
Women gain the right to vote nationwide.
The United States sends combat troops to Vietnam; the last withdraw in 1973.

Event: United States in World War I
Description: The United States enters the war on the side of the Allies in April 1917.
The United States fights Britain over trade restrictions and the impressment of American sailors.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Federalist Age

Description: Pope Gregory the Great sends Augustine to convert the Anglo-Saxons to Christianity.
James II is deposed and William III and Mary II take the throne; the Bill of Rights follows in 1689.
Constantine and Licinius grant toleration to Christians in the Roman Empire.
Parliament taxes printed materials in the colonies, provoking widespread protest.
Historical Periods: Revolutionary and Early National Period; Revolutionary Age

Description: The United States and the Soviet Union compete for global power.
A nine-day strike in support of coal miners halts much of the country.
An outpouring of African American art, music and literature centered in Harlem, New York.
Potato blight causes mass starvation and emigration from Ireland.
The last Tudor monarch presides over a golden age of English drama and poetry.

Event: United States in World War II
Description: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, brings the United States into the war.
Rebels led by Wat Tyler march on London over taxation and serfdom.
Mechanized industry, steam power and factories transform British society.
Martin Luther posts his Ninety-five Theses in Wittenberg.
The Archbishop of Canterbury is killed in his cathedral; his shrine becomes England's great pilgrimage site.
The Supreme Court rules that Black Americans cannot be citizens and that Congress cannot ban slavery in the territories.
